# saveme

> saveme is a Python toolkit (standard library only) for Linux snapshots and encrypted archive disks. `snapmgr` takes btrfs and zfs snapshots and thins them by an age policy such as `0-1dy: all, 1dy-1wk: 4hr, 1wk+: none`; `disktool` prepares LUKS-encrypted ext4 archive disks; `mirroradm` (indexing and checksums toward backups) is unfinished. Every root action is a short bash script that prints the commands it would run; the tools show them and ask before running unless `--noprompt` is given. saveme does not encrypt snapshots, and snapshots are not a backup by themselves.

Every page below is Markdown. llms-full.txt has all of them in one file.

## Start here

- [Overview](index.md): what each tool does and how it runs
- [Getting started](getting-started.md): the tree, the scripts, a walkthrough, design philosophy

## Use
